keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Achaemenid Empire shape of 350 holds all of it). The Phoenicia region (50 cells, about 12,600 km2) and the Cyprus island region (30 cells, about 7,600 km2) stand for the rebels' ground; the Tennes page names Phoenicia and Sidon, and says Anatolia and Cyprus rulers 'also followed the revolt' without naming them or dating them. No area on the pages.

correction.text: Cyprus alone, the last rebel ground

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Sidon's fall only Cyprus remains. The pages do not date the Cyprus reduction; 343 is the year Idrieus was given the task.

region.text: Phoenicia, with Sidon as its centre

ledger.note: 350 BCE: Phoenicia rises against Artaxerxes III under Tennes of Sidon. 'Soon after the failure of the Egyptian campaign of the Achaemenid ruler Artaxerxes III, the Phoenicians declared their independence from Persian rule'; the Egyptian failure is 'around 351 BC' (Artaxerxes III page). No page dates the revolt; 350 is the achaemenid-empire dossier's year.

350 BCE: Phoenicia is free of Persian rule. Phoenicia, from which the Persian forces were driven out; Tennes 'was aided by 4,000 Greek mercenaries sent to him by Nectanebo II and commanded by Mentor of Rhodes'.
350 BCE: Cyprus joins. 'Soon after this Egyptian defeat, Phoenicia, Anatolia and Cyprus declared their independence from Persian rule.' The page names no Cypriot king and gives no year.
350 BCE: the revolt begins; 'Artaxerxes personally led an army of 330,000 men against Sidon' (undated on the page; the Sidon page has Phoenicia 'invaded by Artaxerxes III' in 351 BC).

346 BCE: Sidon falls and Phoenicia is retaken. The Mentor of Rhodes page has the resistance 'unable to defeat Artaxerxes' army' and 'captured in 346 BC'; the Tennes page: 'Sidon was then burnt to the ground, either by Artaxerxes or by the Sidonian citizens' and Tennes 'put to death by Artaxerxes III in 346-345 BC'.
343 BCE: Cyprus is reduced. 'In 343 BC, Artaxerxes committed responsibility for the suppression of the Cyprian rebels to Idrieus'; 'Idrieus succeeded in reducing Cyprus' (undated).
343 BCE: the last rebel ground is taken. The Egyptian reconquest follows ('probably in 340 or 339 BC' on the Artaxerxes III page; 343 elsewhere).

343 BCE: the revolt is over; the land returns to the Achaemenid Empire. 'In the course of a few years Mentor and his forces were able to bring the whole Asian Mediterranean coast into complete submission and dependence.'

wars.name: Revolt of Phoenicia and Cyprus against Artaxerxes III
wars.outcome: Sidon was burnt and Tennes put to death (346-345); Idrieus of Caria was given the Cyprus campaign in 343 and reduced the island. Nectanebo II sent 4,000 Greek mercenaries under Mentor of Rhodes to Tennes; Mentor was captured in 346 and later served Artaxerxes.
wars.note: Dates are the achaemenid-empire dossier's 350-343 on the Artaxerxes III page; the Tennes page gives only 351-346.

certainty.note: No page gives the rebels' frontiers; the Phoenicia and Cyprus regions stand in.

notes: Four pages (budget 2-5). The pages are thin on the dates of the Sidonian revolt: Tennes page r. c. 351 - c. 346 and execution 346-345; Sidon page an invasion in 351; Artaxerxes III page no year for the revolt or Sidon's fall, Cyprus 343; Mentor page capture 346. The start (350) and the Phoenician end (346) are therefore confidence 1-2. Anatolia is named among the rebels on the Artaxerxes III page but no state or date is given. The Cypriot kings (Evagoras II of Salamis, Pnytagoras) are not on any page opened. The slug is the one achaemenid-empire already uses for its contest pair. The Egyptian reconquest date differs on the Artaxerxes III page (probably 340 or 339) and in the achaemenid-empire dossier (343).
